headline: RBA deputy spooks markets with "materially worse" inflation warning as oil tumbles nearly 4% and GOOG earnings loom on Oct 28.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: GOOG slipped 1.1% last night as investors get cautious ahead of its October 28 earnings report. There's some nervousness around ongoing legal risks (antitrust cases) and whether Google Cloud growth can justify the valuation. The long-term AI story remains intact — earnings next week will be the real test.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO nudged up 0.87% last night, a small positive move with no major catalyst. GTA 6 launch speculation continues to swirl — some reports flag PS5 platform uncertainty but most analysts see this as noise ahead of what should be a blockbuster release. Still in the red overall, but the long-term thesis around GTA 6 hasn't changed.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI nudged up 0.24% today in a quiet session. AI stocks have had a rough patch recently — the ETF is still down about 12.7% on your cost base — but the sector news is broadly positive with Google's Gemini 4 Carbon and continued AI model competition. Long-term, this is a high-conviction theme; short-term volatility is the cost of admission.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: MSFT was essentially flat last night, down just 0.3%. Guggenheim reiterated its Buy rating ahead of Microsoft's October 28 earnings. The stock is up 20% on your cost base — one of your strongest performers. Earnings next week will be closely watched for Azure and AI Copilot revenue growth.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS dipped another 0.68% at today's close. China's Tianqi Lithium flagged a 25%+ quarter-on-quarter profit slump in Q3, which weighs on lithium sentiment broadly. PLS is down 56.8% on your cost base — a painful position. There's no quick fix while lithium prices stay depressed, but the long-term EV battery demand story remains the investment case.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE slipped 0.33% today. Emerging market sentiment is softly negative amid Middle East tension and a stronger AUD (which can reduce the AUD value of overseas holdings). Down 3.3% on cost base — nothing alarming for a long-term diversified holding.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG edged up 0.15% today in a quiet session. No specific news catalyst — just tracking the broad market. Slightly underwater on cost base (-1.74%) but that's rounding error territory for a diversified fund. Steady as she goes.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS gained 0.14% today, reflecting the modest positive tone in US markets from last night's S&P 500 session. Up 4.5% on cost base. A quiet, solid performer doing exactly what it's supposed to.

movers.name: DHHF
movers.note: DHHF was basically flat today, down just 0.05%. Essentially break-even on your cost base. No news of note — this broad global ETF just tracks the overall market. Nothing to see here.

watch_today.title: GOOG & MSFT earnings on Oct 28 — big week ahead
watch_today.detail: Both Alphabet and Microsoft report earnings on October 28 (US time). That's your two biggest US holdings. For GOOG, analysts are watching Google Cloud growth and whether AI investment is paying off. For MSFT, the focus is Azure revenue and Copilot AI subscription uptake. Guggenheim reiterated a Buy on MSFT. Expect some pre-earnings volatility — as a long-term holder, sit tight and let the results speak.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Hold into earnings next week
watch_today.detail: MSFT is up 20% on your cost base and barely moved last night (-0.31%). The stock is in strong shape heading into October 28 earnings. Guggenheim's Buy reaffirmation is a good sign. No reason to do anything — just watch for the result.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Lithium pain continues — hold, don't panic
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals dipped again today and is down 56.8% on your cost base. China's Tianqi Lithium just reported a 25%+ quarter-on-quarter profit slump, which keeps sentiment negative across the lithium sector. The bull case — EV battery demand driving lithium prices higher — is delayed, not dead. Selling now would lock in a big loss at the worst point of the cycle. Hold unless your thesis has fundamentally changed.

watch_today.title: RBA rate hike risk rising — watch your mortgage
watch_today.detail: The RBA's deputy governor warned today that the inflation outlook is 'materially worse', and markets have quickly priced in a higher chance of a fifth interest rate hike this year. If you have a variable-rate mortgage, this is worth watching. Higher rates also put pressure on growth stocks and property. Keep an eye on the RBA decision date.

watch_today.title: Oil down nearly 4% — good for inflation, watch energy exposure
watch_today.detail: Crude oil (WTI) dropped from $101.79 to $97.74 last night — a fall of nearly 4%. Lower oil is generally good for inflation and could take some pressure off the RBA. It may also soften the case for further rate hikes if it sticks. No direct impact on your portfolio, but a tailwind for the broader economy.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX: Bumpy ride, but the AI theme is alive — hold
watch_today.detail: Your AI ETF ticked up 0.24% today but is still down 12.7% on cost base. The news flow around AI is overwhelmingly positive — Google launching Gemini 4 Carbon this month, DeepSeek opening new tools, intense competition between Claude, GPT-6 and Gemini. The volatility in AI stocks is real, but the long-term growth story is intact. Hold.

world.summary: The big global stories today centre on escalating Middle East tensions, US midterm election interference fears, a major Arctic strategy shift, and a Nigerian first at the global cancer body.

stories.title: Netanyahu pressing for major new strikes on Iran as tensions escalate
stories.why_it_matters: Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu is actively pushing plans for major new military strikes on Iran, with the Financial Times reporting he made preparations to restart strikes earlier this month. Iran has responded by repeating threats to attack undersea fibre-optic cables — the physical infrastructure that carries most of the world's internet traffic. An escalation here could spike oil prices (already elevated around $97/barrel), disrupt global communications, and rattle financial markets. This is the most volatile geopolitical flashpoint in the world right now.

stories.title: Trump steps up threats over US midterm elections — federal officials quietly warn states
stories.why_it_matters: With two weeks until the US midterm elections, Trump is ramping up threats around election integrity, and US federal officials are now privately briefing state governments on how to handle potential interference. In California, the Trump administration is pursuing a lawsuit to throw out 20,000 ballots — a judge called it 'bordering on the absurd'. This level of pre-election legal and political turmoil is unusual even by recent US standards, and the outcome will shape control of Congress and US policy direction for the next two years.

stories.title: EU shifts Arctic strategy to focus on security and geopolitical competition
stories.why_it_matters: The European Union has released a new Arctic strategy that marks a significant shift — away from purely environmental concerns and toward security and geopolitical competition. With Russia's presence in the Arctic and China's growing interest in Arctic shipping routes and resources, the EU is now treating the region as a strategic frontier. This matters because the Arctic holds vast untapped energy and mineral resources, and control of future shipping lanes could reshape global trade.

stories.title: Nigerian breaks global barrier — takes charge of world cancer control body
stories.why_it_matters: A Nigerian has become the first African to lead the world's top cancer control organisation — a historic milestone in global health leadership. Africa carries a disproportionate burden of cancer deaths, often diagnosed late due to lack of screening and treatment infrastructure. Having African leadership at the top of global cancer governance could shift funding priorities and research focus toward diseases and challenges most affecting lower-income countries.

stories.title: Global economic outlook darkens — autumn 2026 review
stories.why_it_matters: The autumn 2026 global economic outlook review flags tightening financial conditions and slowing growth across major economies. The combination of sticky inflation, elevated interest rates in the US and Australia, and ongoing geopolitical disruptions (Middle East, Ukraine) is making central banks' jobs harder. For Australian investors, this means the 'higher for longer' interest rate environment isn't going away quickly, and global growth headwinds could weigh on equity markets into 2027.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 finished today's session up a modest 0.16%, while last night the S&P 500 gained 0.28% and the NASDAQ was essentially flat. The big market story is oil, which tumbled nearly 4% last night to below $98 — a meaningful drop that could ease inflation pressure. Gold is holding near all-time highs around $4,145. The Aussie dollar bounced strongly, up 0.77% to 70.4 US cents.

politics.summary: The RBA's deputy governor has rattled markets with a stark warning that Australia's inflation outlook is 'materially worse', sharply lifting the odds of a fifth interest rate hike this year. Meanwhile, Labor is staring down a growing budget hole.

stories.title: RBA deputy warns inflation outlook 'materially worse' — fifth rate hike odds surge
stories.why_it_matters: The RBA's deputy governor spoke today and caught markets off guard, warning that the inflation outlook has become 'materially worse'. This has caused the market odds of a fifth interest rate hike in 2026 to double almost overnight, according to The Guardian. If the RBA does raise rates again, it means higher mortgage repayments for millions of Australians on variable-rate home loans, and higher borrowing costs for businesses. The next RBA decision is being watched very closely — rate rise bets have jumped sharply.

stories.title: Labor faces $11 billion budget hole from backflips, delays and rising bond yields
stories.why_it_matters: The AFR reports the Albanese government is now facing an $11 billion hole in its budget, caused by a combination of policy backflips, spending delays, and the cost of rising bond yields (the government's borrowing costs going up as interest rates stay elevated). This limits Labor's room to manoeuvre on new spending promises and could force some tough choices before the next election. It also adds to fiscal pressure at a time when the RBA is already worried about inflation.

stories.title: Explainer: What the RBA cash rate actually is, and how it hits your mortgage
stories.why_it_matters: With rate hike fears back in the spotlight, Ticker News has published a plain-English explainer on how the RBA cash rate works and how changes flow through to home loan repayments. The short version: when the RBA lifts the cash rate, banks quickly pass on higher rates to variable mortgage holders, meaning your monthly repayments rise. Fixed-rate borrowers are shielded until their fixed term ends. Worth a read if you're fuzzy on the mechanics.

ai.summary: Big week for AI news — Google's next-generation Gemini 4 Carbon is reportedly dropping this month, DeepSeek is opening a new inference platform to challenge OpenAI and Anthropic, and the UN is raising the alarm about AI increasingly crowding out human decision-making in warfare.

stories.title: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon arriving this month with major upgrades
stories.why_it_matters: Google is reportedly launching Gemini 4 Carbon — its next major AI model — this month, with significant upgrades over the current version. This is directly relevant to your GOOG holding: Google's ability to stay competitive in AI against OpenAI, Anthropic, and DeepSeek is central to its future revenue and market position. Gemini 4 Carbon is expected to be more capable at complex reasoning and multimodal tasks (meaning it can work across text, images, video and audio together). A strong launch could be a catalyst for the stock ahead of earnings.

stories.title: DeepSeek launches DeepInfer, pressing hard on OpenAI and Anthropic
stories.why_it_matters: China's DeepSeek has opened a new platform called DeepInfer, directly targeting OpenAI and Anthropic's turf. DeepSeek has consistently punched above its weight — releasing models that rival the best Western AI at a fraction of the cost. Reports put the price gap between leading AI models at up to 20x, with DeepSeek at the cheap end. This keeps competitive pressure intense on Google, Microsoft/OpenAI and Anthropic — good for consumers (cheaper AI), but it means none of the big players can rest.

stories.title: UN warns AI is 'crowding out' human decision-making in warfare
stories.why_it_matters: The United Nations has released a report warning that AI is increasingly being used to make or inform lethal decisions in military conflicts, and that human oversight is being 'crowded out'. Autonomous weapons and AI-assisted targeting are moving faster than the international rules designed to govern them. This is a big-picture risk — both ethically and in terms of potential for miscalculation and escalation in conflict zones like the Middle East.

stories.title: Claude Opus 5.5 vs GPT-6 Astra: The AI model wars heat up
stories.why_it_matters: Benchmark testing comparing Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 against OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra shows them neck-and-neck on complex coding and reasoning tasks, with Claude scoring 66% on the Terminal-Bench test. The broader AI price war is also intensifying — reports show the cost gap between the most expensive and cheapest frontier AI models has hit 20x. This rapid commoditisation of AI is great for businesses using it, but squeezes margins for the companies building it.

stories.title: Governments wrestling with how to regulate AI — and the rule book is still being written
stories.why_it_matters: Both US states and international bodies are scrambling to write AI regulation, but the technology is moving faster than the lawmakers. Science News reports that the fundamental question — how do you assess whether an AI system is safe before it's deployed? — still has no agreed answer. Several US states are pushing their own rules in the absence of federal legislation, creating a patchwork of requirements that will be costly for AI companies to navigate and could favour large players who can absorb compliance costs.

sport.summary: NRL Grand Final done — Roosters over Knights 19-18. The Rugby League World Cup is underway, Australia's Kangaroos have a new captain, and the PNG Chiefs have unveiled their inaugural NRL logo ahead of their historic entry into the competition.

stories.title: Roosters win NRL Grand Final 19-18 over the Knights in a thriller
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters claimed the 2026 NRL premiership in a nail-biting one-point win over the Newcastle Knights — 19 to 18 — at Accor Stadium. It doesn't get much tighter than that. A single point separated two clubs at the end of the season, which makes it one of the closest Grand Finals in recent memory. Big result for Roosters fans on the Gold Coast.

stories.title: Tedesco named Kangaroos captain for first Test since 2023
stories.why_it_matters: James Tedesco has been parachuted in as Kangaroos captain for Australia's first international Test match since 2023, as the Rugby League World Cup kicks off. Tedesco, the Roosters fullback and freshly minted premiership winner, takes the armband in what shapes as a significant statement of faith from selectors. Australia hasn't played a Test in over two years, so this is a big moment for the national team.

stories.title: PNG Chiefs unveil inaugural logo and jersey — NRL's 'watershed' moment
stories.why_it_matters: The Papua New Guinea Chiefs have officially unveiled their inaugural logo and jersey, ahead of joining the NRL as an expansion team. Fox Sports called it a 'watershed' moment for the game — PNG is rugby league mad, and a dedicated NRL team represents a massive step in the sport's Pacific expansion. The jerseys and branding were met with strong public reaction in PNG.

stories.title: Rugby League World Cup 2026 — Women's Round 2 team lists and updates
stories.why_it_matters: The 2026 Rugby League World Cup women's competition is into Round 2, with official team lists and injury updates now out. The women's World Cup has grown enormously in profile over recent tournaments — this is now a serious showcase for the game globally. Check NRL.com for the full team lists and any late changes before the matches.

stories.title: NRL signings tracker: Sanders, Paulo, Kelly ink new deals
stories.why_it_matters: The off-season signing frenzy is in full swing. NRL.com's tracker confirms that Sanders, Paulo, and Kelly have all put pen to paper on new deals, while a young gun is reportedly leaving the Titans amid a $3 million chase from rival clubs. The player market is heating up as clubs lock in their rosters for 2027.
